detectors.rationale: Setting csrf.checkOrigin: false in svelte.config.js turns off SvelteKit's built-in same-origin check for form-content-type POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE requests, so any external site can submit forms to this app's actions on a victim's behalf; the safe idiom simply omits the csrf block, leaving checkOrigin at its documented default of true, which the regex (anchored on the literal `false` value) correctly does not match.

SvelteKit resolves csrf_check_origin to true only when checkOrigin is true AND trustedOrigins does not contain '*'; trustedOrigins: ['*'] silently disables the origin check for every request regardless of checkOrigin, defeating CSRF protection entirely. The safe idiom names specific trusted origins (e.g. 'https://trusted-partner.example.com'), which the wildcard-anchored regex correctly does not match.

Passing the raw cookies.get('sessionid') value directly into a database lookup with no verification step means any forged or guessed cookie value returns a full account record — there is no authentication, only an unguarded lookup. The safe idiom resolves and verifies the session through a requireLogin(event) call first and only queries the database with the verified user id, which the regex (anchored on a db call receiving cookies.get(...) as a direct argument) correctly does not match.

Explicitly setting httpOnly: false on a session cookie makes it readable from client-side JavaScript, so any XSS elsewhere in the app (or an injected third-party script) can exfiltrate the live session token. The safe idiom sets httpOnly: true alongside secure and sameSite, matching SvelteKit's documented cookie defaults, which the httpOnly:false-anchored regex correctly does not match.

Binding {@html comment.body} sets innerHTML directly from user-submitted markup with no sanitization, allowing stored XSS for every viewer of the comment. The safe idiom pipes the same value through DOMPurify.sanitize(comment.body) inline in the template expression; the regex (a bare identifier/property chain with no call syntax before the closing brace) correctly does not match the sanitizer-call form.
